- Debt/Equity improved from 0.87x (FY22) to 0.15x (FY26), with net worth growing from Rs 202 Cr to Rs 778 Cr over the same period.

bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Export leadership in the US: largest exporter of low-voltage cables (up to 600V) from India to the US in CY2025, with the highest total export share among leading Indian wire and cable companies, eight active US distributors (up from two in FY 2021-22) and a zero-rejection track record for six consecutive years.
- Approvals and certification moat: UL, LPCB, BIS, RDSO, NTPC, PGCIL and EIL approvals secured over years act as qualification barriers in institutional and export markets.
- Distribution reach: over 250 channel partners, 600+ retail outlets, more than 10,000 registered electricians via the Paramount Parivaar loyalty platform, and e-commerce presence on recognised portals.
- Institutional franchise: more than 950 institutional clients across diverse sectors with long-standing relationships, giving revenue stability and mitigating sector-specific demand fluctuations.
- Product breadth and pioneering record: six product categories plus EPC; first in India with lead-free house wires, axle counter cables for Indian Railways and fire survival cables, and among early movers in submarine cable laying and repair.
- Capacity fungibility: ability to redirect production between domestic and export markets, demonstrated by a 43% export mix in H1 FY26 shifting to an 84% domestic mix in H2 FY26 after the US tariff shock.
- Diversified geography: presence across 35+ export geographies and Pan-India domestic coverage.
- Financial discipline: robust financial position and net worth with low debt, enabling the Company to capitalise on new opportunities.
- Experienced management and long operating history: nearly seven decades of track record; leadership that has navigated market cycles and external disruptions.
- In-house R&D and quality infrastructure: R&D focused on application-specific and higher-value-added products, with computerised testing laboratories and stage-wise quality checks. (Note: the BRSR states the Company 'does not currently have a dedicated Research and Development (R&D) function', which conflicts with the MD&A description of a well-structured in-house R&D team.)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Export / trade-policy and US tariff concentration — The US is Paramount's largest export destination and exports were about 28.9% of FY2025-26 sales; the AR states export performance was impacted by the increase in US import tariffs, which temporarily affected margins, and the Chairman describes 'unprecedented disruptions following changes in United States (US) tariff policies'.
- Raw material price volatility (copper, aluminium, steel, PVC) — MD&A Raw Material Risk: price volatility of key raw materials alongside potential supply disruption, shortages or delays may exert pressure on margins, impacting operational and financial performance; mitigated by structured inventory management and calibrated pricing.
- Competition risk — MD&A: competition from domestic and global market participants poses challenges to the Company's pricing strategy and competitive position; mitigated by technological capability, diversified portfolio, certifications and brand equity.
- Currency fluctuation risk — MD&A: exposure to foreign exchange rates arising from imports of raw materials and exports of finished products; volatile rates impact margins, partly offset by a natural hedge and forward contracts.
- Customer concentration risk — MD&A Concentration Risk: excessive reliance on a limited number of customers could adversely affect revenues and profitability; BRSR adds that sales to the top 10 dealers/distributors were 82.71% of total sales to dealers/distributors in FY 2025-26.
- Macro-economic and geopolitical risk — MD&A: economic slowdown, geopolitical developments and inflationary pressure may weaken demand and affect production, revenue and performance; MD&A separately flags Middle East tensions disrupting the Red Sea / Suez routes, raising freight costs and copper/aluminium price volatility.
- Technology obsolescence risk — MD&A: failure to keep pace with technological developments or meet customer-specific technical and quality requirements can adversely affect orders and market competitiveness.
- Statutory compliance and product quality / safety risk — MD&A Statutory Compliance Risk warns of fines, legal penalties and licence revocation; the BRSR material-issues table separately flags Product Quality & Safety, where inadequate quality or non-compliance may result in product recalls, regulatory action, financial liabilities and reputational damage.

outlook.body:

- Deepen export diversification: strengthen existing geographies (US, UK, Myanmar, Nepal and 35+ countries) while exploring new and emerging markets, and expand the overseas distributor network.

- Accelerate investments in employee training and capability development.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY 2025-26 marked the beginning of Paramount's major investment cycle, with its two existing manufacturing units at Kushkhera (Rajasthan) and Dharuhera (Haryana) described as operating at near-optimal utilisation over the past several years. During the year the Company initiated development of a third, greenfield manufacturing facility at Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh, spread across 31 acres and being developed with an investment of approximately Rs 300 crore. Civil works and site preparation are underway and orders for long-lead plant and machinery have been placed. The plant will enable entry into Extra High Voltage (EHV) cables up to 132 kV, and initially specialised transmission conductors, elastomeric e-beam cables and other specialised cables, broadening the addressable market in power transmission infrastructure. Management expects partial commissioning during Q1 FY28 followed by a phased ramp-up through the year, and a targeted revenue of Rs 1,200 crore with total investment of Rs 300 crore over the next two to three years from this plant. Alongside the greenfield project, the Company reports continued investment in automation, digital monitoring, quality systems, equipment upgrades and energy optimisation; the BRSR notes investment in advanced machinery, testing equipment and energy-efficient generators. Capacity fungibility across units lets the Company redirect production between domestic and export markets as conditions change.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Power infrastructure and renewable energy: continued investment in generation, transmission and distribution, smart grids, Green Energy Corridors and solar/wind projects remain the primary demand drivers; the Government's 500 GW non-fossil capacity target by 2030 is creating long-term demand for EHV power cables.
- Government T&D spending: Rs 3.35 lakh crore earmarked for transmission and distribution infrastructure over FY 2025-26 to FY 2029-30, PGCIL planning over Rs 1 lakh crore of network expansion, the Rs 3 lakh crore RDSS programme, and a CEA transmission pipeline exceeding Rs 7 lakh crore through 2036.
- Railway infrastructure: a record Union Budget 2026-27 capital outlay of Rs 2,93,030 crore for Indian Railways, with electrification, signalling upgrades and freight corridors driving demand for railway signalling, power and communication cables.
- Data centres and AI: India's data centre capacity rose from about 375 MW in 2020 to around 1,500 MW by 2025 and is expected to expand from the current 1.7 GW to over 8 GW by 2030, with the Ministry of Power estimating data-centre electricity demand reaching 13.56 GW by 2031-32.
- Telecom and digital connectivity: 5G rollout, FTTH deployment and low fibreisation of telecom towers support demand for optical fibre and communication cables; communication cables are projected to grow at a 12.38% CAGR through 2031.
- Formalisation of the industry: mandatory BIS certification, stricter quality standards and a preference for branded products lifted the organised segment to around 74% of the market in 2025, supporting share gains for organised manufacturers.
- Export opportunity: India's wire and cable exports are projected to grow at around a 14% CAGR over FY2025-FY2030; the US wires and cables market is USD 32 billion with USD 1 trillion of planned grid investment through 2030.
- Market size: the India wire and cable market is estimated at USD 21.22 billion in 2025 growing to USD 35.58 billion by 2031 at a 9.01% CAGR.
- Margin headwinds: EBITDA and profitability moderated on temporary US tariff-related uncertainties, certain one-time items, and one-time cost from the new labour codes notified in November 2025.
- Mix: power cables now account for the largest share of the product portfolio, with the institutional (B2B) business growing 37.3% and retail growing more than 25% in FY 2025-26.
- Segment outlook: railway cable demand supported by the Government's commitment to 100% railway electrification; house wires supported by housing, construction and renovation demand plus rising electrical-safety awareness.
- As of March 31, 2026, the Company had a pending order book of more than Rs 583.3 crore, comprising domestic cables of Rs 507.8 crore and exports of Rs 75.5 crore.
- Order book mix disclosed as 87% domestic and 13% export.

currentContext.expansion: FY 2025-26 marked the beginning of Paramount's major investment cycle, with its two existing manufacturing units at Kushkhera (Rajasthan) and Dharuhera (Haryana) described as operating at near-optimal utilisation over the past several years. During the year the Company initiated development of a third, greenfield manufacturing facility at Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh, spread across 31 acres and being developed with an investment of approximately Rs 300 crore. Civil works and site preparation are underway and orders for long-lead plant and machinery have been placed. The plant will enable entry into Extra High Voltage (EHV) cables up to 132 kV, and initially specialised transmission conductors, elastomeric e-beam cables and other specialised cables, broadening the addressable market in power transmission infrastructure. Management expects partial commissioning during Q1 FY28 followed by a phased ramp-up through the year, and a targeted revenue of Rs 1,200 crore with total investment of Rs 300 crore over the next two to three years from this plant. Alongside the greenfield project, the Company reports continued investment in automation, digital monitoring, quality systems, equipment upgrades and energy optimisation; the BRSR notes investment in advanced machinery, testing equipment and energy-efficient generators. Capacity fungibility across units lets the Company redirect production between domestic and export markets as conditions change.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Power infrastructure and renewable energy: continued investment in generation, transmission and distribution, smart grids, Green Energy Corridors and solar/wind projects remain the primary demand drivers; the Government's 500 GW non-fossil capacity target by 2030 is creating long-term demand for EHV power cables.
- Government T&D spending: Rs 3.35 lakh crore earmarked for transmission and distribution infrastructure over FY 2025-26 to FY 2029-30, PGCIL planning over Rs 1 lakh crore of network expansion, the Rs 3 lakh crore RDSS programme, and a CEA transmission pipeline exceeding Rs 7 lakh crore through 2036.
- Railway infrastructure: a record Union Budget 2026-27 capital outlay of Rs 2,93,030 crore for Indian Railways, with electrification, signalling upgrades and freight corridors driving demand for railway signalling, power and communication cables.
- Data centres and AI: India's data centre capacity rose from about 375 MW in 2020 to around 1,500 MW by 2025 and is expected to expand from the current 1.7 GW to over 8 GW by 2030, with the Ministry of Power estimating data-centre electricity demand reaching 13.56 GW by 2031-32.
- Telecom and digital connectivity: 5G rollout, FTTH deployment and low fibreisation of telecom towers support demand for optical fibre and communication cables; communication cables are projected to grow at a 12.38% CAGR through 2031.
- Formalisation of the industry: mandatory BIS certification, stricter quality standards and a preference for branded products lifted the organised segment to around 74% of the market in 2025, supporting share gains for organised manufacturers.
- Export opportunity: India's wire and cable exports are projected to grow at around a 14% CAGR over FY2025-FY2030; the US wires and cables market is USD 32 billion with USD 1 trillion of planned grid investment through 2030.
- Market size: the India wire and cable market is estimated at USD 21.22 billion in 2025 growing to USD 35.58 billion by 2031 at a 9.01% CAGR.
- Margin headwinds: EBITDA and profitability moderated on temporary US tariff-related uncertainties, certain one-time items, and one-time cost from the new labour codes notified in November 2025.
- Mix: power cables now account for the largest share of the product portfolio, with the institutional (B2B) business growing 37.3% and retail growing more than 25% in FY 2025-26.
- Segment outlook: railway cable demand supported by the Government's commitment to 100% railway electrification; house wires supported by housing, construction and renovation demand plus rising electrical-safety awareness.
- As of March 31, 2026, the Company had a pending order book of more than Rs 583.3 crore, comprising domestic cables of Rs 507.8 crore and exports of Rs 75.5 crore.
- Order book mix disclosed as 87% domestic and 13% export.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin down to 8.5% in FY25 from 9% due to lower realized prices from falling copper/aluminum commodity costs (metal price decline offset volume growth); Q4 margin dipped to 6.6% due to strategic volume ramp-up and tariff transition costs in US; cost structure remains leveraged to metal input, but working capital efficiency offsets pressure

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY 2025-26 marked the beginning of Paramount's major investment cycle, with its two existing manufacturing units at Kushkhera (Rajasthan) and Dharuhera (Haryana) described as operating at near-optimal utilisation over the past several years. During the year the Company initiated development of a third, greenfield manufacturing facility at Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh, spread across 31 acres and being developed with an investment of approximately Rs 300 crore. Civil works and site preparation are underway and orders for long-lead plant and machinery have been placed. The plant will enable entry into Extra High Voltage (EHV) cables up to 132 kV, and initially specialised transmission conductors, elastomeric e-beam cables and other specialised cables, broadening the addressable market in power transmission infrastructure. Management expects partial commissioning during Q1 FY28 followed by a phased ramp-up through the year, and a targeted revenue of Rs 1,200 crore with total investment of Rs 300 crore over the next two to three years from this plant. Alongside the greenfield project, the Company reports continued investment in automation, digital monitoring, quality systems, equipment upgrades and energy optimisation; the BRSR notes investment in advanced machinery, testing equipment and energy-efficient generators. Capacity fungibility across units lets the Company redirect production between domestic and export markets as conditions change.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, pragmatic, and outcome-focused; CEO prioritizes absolute rupee profit over margin percentages; dismisses ‘new normal’ margin narratives; emphasizes flexibility, volume-driven growth, and shareholder returns; acknowledges tariff risks but expresses confidence in market position and customer loyalty

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Export leadership in the US: largest exporter of low-voltage cables (up to 600V) from India to the US in CY2025, with the highest total export share among leading Indian wire and cable companies, eight active US distributors (up from two in FY 2021-22) and a zero-rejection track record for six consecutive years.
- Approvals and certification moat: UL, LPCB, BIS, RDSO, NTPC, PGCIL and EIL approvals secured over years act as qualification barriers in institutional and export markets.
- Distribution reach: over 250 channel partners, 600+ retail outlets, more than 10,000 registered electricians via the Paramount Parivaar loyalty platform, and e-commerce presence on recognised portals.
- Institutional franchise: more than 950 institutional clients across diverse sectors with long-standing relationships, giving revenue stability and mitigating sector-specific demand fluctuations.
- Product breadth and pioneering record: six product categories plus EPC; first in India with lead-free house wires, axle counter cables for Indian Railways and fire survival cables, and among early movers in submarine cable laying and repair.
- Capacity fungibility: ability to redirect production between domestic and export markets, demonstrated by a 43% export mix in H1 FY26 shifting to an 84% domestic mix in H2 FY26 after the US tariff shock.
- Diversified geography: presence across 35+ export geographies and Pan-India domestic coverage.
- Financial discipline: robust financial position and net worth with low debt, enabling the Company to capitalise on new opportunities.
- Experienced management and long operating history: nearly seven decades of track record; leadership that has navigated market cycles and external disruptions.
- In-house R&D and quality infrastructure: R&D focused on application-specific and higher-value-added products, with computerised testing laboratories and stage-wise quality checks. (Note: the BRSR states the Company 'does not currently have a dedicated Research and Development (R&D) function', which conflicts with the MD&A description of a well-structured in-house R&D team.)

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: US tariff volatility (current duty: 14%-15%, potential reciprocal duties post-July 8); metal price volatility; execution risk at new plant; over-reliance on US market (95% of exports); working capital discipline may constrain growth if domestic demand surges

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Despite 57% metal volume growth, revenue grew only 47% — indicating commodity price deflation, not product mix shift; working capital reduction from 155 to 101 days was achieved by reducing exposure to slow-paying government clients; export order book is deliberately kept lean (~50% of total) to preserve capacity flexibility for higher-margin opportunities

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen domestic leadership and expand presence in high-growth infrastructure sectors as stated FY 2026-27 priorities.
- Restore profitability to pre-tariff levels as export markets normalise.
- Commission the Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh greenfield facility and move up into Extra High Voltage cables, specialised transmission conductors and elastomeric e-beam cables.
- Maintain manufacturing fungibility so capacity can be redirected between export and domestic markets as conditions change - demonstrated by a 43% export mix in H1 FY26 and an 84% domestic mix in H2 FY26 after the US tariff …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [US tariff shock] An August 2025 US tariff shock drove a sharp swing in channel mix: export share fell from 43% in H1 FY26 to 16% in H2 FY26 (domestic pivot to 84%), before recovering to 29% export share in Q1 FY27 as tariff uncertainty eased.
